title: The Artist's Way
note: DB Turkish title 'Yaratıcı Beyin' is not a faithful title. Full text is borrow-only on archive.org, not accessible. Facts rely on consistent quotations in secondary sources and Cameron's own site; confidence capped at medium. The book gives tools and concepts, not one dated event, so all three stories are concept stories.

facts.claim: Morning pages: three pages of longhand writing, strictly stream-of-consciousness, written first thing in the morning.
facts.source: The Muse quoting the book; multiple secondary

facts.claim: There is no wrong way to do morning pages; they are not high art; no topic is too trivial.
By spilling out of bed straight onto the page every morning, you learn to evade the Censor; because there is no wrong way, the Censor's opinion does not count.
Cameron advises not rereading the pages, and not letting anyone else read them, at least for the first eight weeks.
Cameron on her own practice: 'I learned to just show up at the page and write down what I heard... I didn't have to be in the mood.'
Cameron began teaching blocked artists in 1978; the work grew from one-on-one sessions to workshops and a course, then the book.

The Censor: a nasty internal and eternal critic. 'Think of your Censor as a cartoon serpent, slithering around your creative Eden, hissing vile things to keep you off guard.' If a serpent doesn't work, draw another cartoon image, perhaps the shark from Jaws, put an X through it, and post it where you write. Making it a nasty clever little character begins to pry loose its power. The Censor's negative opinion is not the truth.
facts.source: multiple secondary quoting the Basic Tools chapter

facts.claim: Week 1 ('Recovering a Sense of Safety') includes listing historic 'monsters' (enemies of your creative self-worth) and 'champions'.
facts.source: multiple reader blogs; PRH table of contents

facts.claim: Artist date: 'a block of time, perhaps two hours weekly, especially set aside and committed to nurturing your creative consciousness, your inner artist.' Done alone. Examples: a great junk store, a solo trip to the beach, an old movie, an aquarium or art gallery.

Filling the well: 'Art is an image-using system.' Making art draws images out of an inner well, ideally like a well-stocked trout pond; without upkeep the well becomes depleted, stagnant or blocked. 'Filling the well involves the active pursuit of images to refresh our artistic reservoirs.' 'In filling the well, think magic. Think delight. Think fun. Do not think duty.' 'Think mystery, not mastery.' Example: if I drive this road, not my usual road, what will I see?
'Morning pages are nonnegotiable. Never skip or skimp on your morning pages.'
facts.source: heroic.us philosopher note quoting the book

facts.claim: 'Beyond the reach of the Censor's babble we find our own quiet center, the place where we hear the still, small voice.' The Censor 'resides in our (left) brain'.
Cameron on students working the process: 'I see a certain amount of defiance and giddiness in the first few weeks.'

Trout-pond passage: 'We've got big fish, little fish, fat fish, skinny fish, an abundance of artistic fish to fry.' And: 'Do what intrigues you, explore what interests you; think mystery, not mastery.'
Pages can hold anything: last night's dreams, plans for the day, things you're excited or worried about.

rejected.claim: Within a few weeks most participants reported surprising changes.
rejected.reason: No measured outcome in the book; unsupported.

rejected.claim: A painter in front of the canvas hears 'Real painters don't do this' and the brush stops.
Quote 'This voice comes from inside, mostly from old injuries.'
Quote 'Creativity gives out and must take in; the one who only gives burns out.'
Many readers find their monsters list short but louder than champions.
rejected.reason: Single reader blog, not the book.
